newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Livshits sees IMF tranche ruling from next mission.
newsitem.headline: Livshits sees IMF tranche ruling from next mission.

text.p: A decision to release an IMF loan tranche to Russia will probably be made when the next monitoring mission arrives in Moscow, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Thursday.
Livshits told Reuters that there were two outstanding issues between Russia and the IMF -- revenues for the 1997 budget, and the structure of economic reforms.
"I think that by the time the next mission arrives, the programme for 1997 will be ready and the question of the current tranche will be solved," he said.
A mission left Russia last week, but the IMF said on Tuesday it was not yet ready to recommend releasing a new tranche of the $10 billion three-year loan.
Livshits did not say when the next mission was due to arrive, but IMF officials have been visiting Russia each month to monitor progress in meeting terms attached to the loan.
A Finance Ministry official said Russia's low tax revenue in January was the main problem.
Livshits saw no problem in relations between Russia and the IMF. "There is no break in our agreement, and our work together is continuing," he said.
